title: Inverse limit on abelian-group towers is additive and left exact
statement: The inverse-limit functor from the category of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] of abelian groups indexed by the natural numbers to abelian groups is additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1 setup for the inverse-limit functor

proof.text: Since morphisms of towers are levelwise, for a morphism of towers u:(A_n)→(B_n) the levelwise kernels ker(u_n), with the transition maps induced by those of (A_n), form a tower which is a kernel of u in the category of towers (the universal property is checked level by level). An element of the inverse limit is a compatible tuple. The kernel of the induced map on limits is therefore the subgroup of compatible tuples whose nth component lies in ker(u_n) for every n; this is exactly the inverse limit of the levelwise kernel tower. Thus the inverse-limit functor preserves kernels.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1 setup and proof of the kernel description

proof.text: Finite biproducts and the zero object in the category of towers are computed levelwise (direct check of the universal properties, morphisms being levelwise). Compatible tuples in a finite biproduct of towers are exactly pairs of compatible tuples, and the zero compatible tuple is unique. Componentwise addition therefore identifies the inverse limit of a finite biproduct with the corresponding biproduct of inverse limits and identifies the inverse limit of the zero tower with zero. Hence inverse limit is additive; together with kernel preservation from the preceding argument, it is left exact by the definition of an additive left exact functor.
